extracted.intended_audience: poets, playwrights, and literary critics (practitioners of creative poetry and drama)
extracted.subtask_short: writing and evaluating poetry and drama
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance for composing and judging poetry and plays: what makes poetry valuable, how verse and form function pedagogically/aesthetically, and practical rules for dramatic composition and comic/tragic tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach and move to virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: No learning is so good as that which teacheth and moveth to virtue; none can both teach and move thereto so much as poesy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate poetry by its moral and educative effect: its capacity both to instruct (docere) and to move/emotionally persuade (movere). Poetry is ranked above history for moral instruction and near to philosophy for instruction-plus-motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry does not assert factual truth (not a lie)
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet never affirmeth; he telleth not for true but what should or should not be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat poetic invention as allegorical or exemplary rather than factual reportage; fictional names and events are permissible to teach or illustrate, and should not be judged as literal falsehoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verse aids memory and learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Verse far exceedeth prose in the knitting up of the memory... every word having his natural seat, which seat must needs make the word remembered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor metrical/ordered language when the goal includes memorability and pedagogical transmission; meter, rhyme, and ordered structure strengthen retention and the teaching function of poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versification alone is insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: One may be a poet without versing, and a versifier without poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not evaluate quality solely by rhyme or measured verse; substantive imagination, moral purpose, and craftsmanship distinguish true poetry from mere versifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet's composition requires art, imitation, and exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: That Dædalus... hath three wings to bear itself up into the air of due commendation; that is art, imitation, and exercise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good poet cultivates (1) art/rules (learned technique), (2) imitation (study and emulation of exemplary models), and (3) disciplined exercise/practice (deliberate work aimed at improvement, not mere repetition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize matter and words coherently
rubrics_metrics.description: There being two principal parts, matter to be expressed by words, and words to express the matter... never marshalling it into any assured rank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure subject matter is well-chosen and structured rather than a scatter of impressions. Marshall and order scenes/arguments so the reader/listener can follow the progression and grasp the central purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain unity of place and time in drama
rubrics_metrics.description: The stage should always represent but one place; and the uttermost time presupposed in it should be... but one day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For effective stage representation, avoid jumping across many locations or compressing long spans of years into one performance; preserve plausibility and audience comprehension by limiting place and time (Aristotelian unities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin at the principal point (not "ab ovo")
rubrics_metrics.description: They must come to the principal point of that one action which they will represent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start the play at the decisive or climactic moment relevant to the action to be shown. Use narrators or messengers (nuntii) to recount earlier or offstage events rather than dramatizing the entire prior history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use narration for offstage or unrepresentable events
rubrics_metrics.description: Many things may be told, which cannot be showed... some 'Nuntius' to recount things done in former time, or other place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When events are impossible or impractical to stage (distant places, lengthy sequences), narrate them instead of attempting implausible stagecraft; rely on reportive devices to preserve unity and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep genres distinct; avoid forced tragi-comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Having indeed no right comedy in that comical part of our tragedy, we have nothing but scurrility... neither the admiration and commiseration, nor the right sportfulness, is by their mongrel tragi-comedy obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain appropriate tonal integrity: do not thrust low comedy into lofty tragic scenes merely for laughs. If mixing comic and tragic elements, do so with skill and deliberation so each purpose (admiration/pity vs. delight/laughter) is preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy must teach delight, not merely provoke laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: All the end of the comical part be not upon such scornful matters as stir laughter only, but mix with that delightful teaching which is the end of poesy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess comedies by their capacity to delight while also instructing or embodying moral lessons. Prefer character-based humor and instructive situations over crude, scornful amusement for its own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid scurrility, indecency, and cruel mockery in comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: They stir laughter in sinful things, which are rather execrable than ridiculous; or in miserable, which are rather to be pitied than scorned... to jest at strangers, because they speak not English so well as we do?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject humor that ridicules poverty, misery, foreigners, or sinful/execrable matters. Target follies and vices (e.g., a self-wise schoolmaster, a heartless Thraso) in ways that produce instructive delight rather than cruel derision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect decorum and plausible representation in staging
rubrics_metrics.description: You shall have Asia of the one side, and Afric of the other... the player, when he comes in, must ever begin with telling where he is... then... a hideous monster with fire and smoke, and then... a cave; while... two armies fly in, represented with four swords and bucklers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid absurd or inconsistent staging that forces the audience into disbelief. Keep settings, props, and scene changes within the plausible limits of the stage and the audience's willingness to imagine; do not overload the stage with incongruous spectacles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid affectation of archaic or rustic diction
rubrics_metrics.description: That same framing of his style to an old rustic language, I dare not allow; since neither Theocritus in Greek, Virgil in Latin, nor Sannazaro in Italian, did affect it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not artificially adopt an archaic or rustic register merely for effect; instead, aim for an idiom suited to the model and purpose of the poem, informed by classical exemplars where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetical originality: make matter, do not merely take it
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet only, only bringeth his own stuff, and doth not learn a conceit out of a matter, but maketh matter for a conceit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value creative invention: poets should generate material imaginatively rather than merely extracting 'subjects' from existing matter. Original shaping of content into exempla and images is central to poetic power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice should be for learning, not mere repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise... where we should exercise to know, we exercise as having known; and so is our brain delivered of much matter which never was begotten by knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage deliberate practice aimed at expanding knowledge and technique. Avoid rote composition that repeats familiar tropes without genuine study or acquisition of new mastery.
